reviewer: Independent quality reviewer; neither Linux implementer nor its specification reviewer

strengths.assessment: One private boolean retains keyboard reveal intent. The existing selected identity remains its single target; the next maintainer need not synchronize a second copied identity or index. The comment explains the delayed snapshot ordering and cleared-selection branch. No shared list API, dependency, schema, persistent setting or native guard changes.

Only vertical navigation sets the flag. Repeated keys update the latest selected PID/start identity while retaining the existing one-frame repaint. At process-table construction, mem::take consumes the flag before selected_index performs full-identity lookup on current rows. List construction and prepaint follow synchronously on the UI thread; no async or yield boundary was introduced. Removed selection cannot retain an application reveal or select a reused PID.

Source inspection: empty tables reject vertical navigation before count-1; a pre-existing pending flag is consumed even with no selection. Collapsed panels do not render a table, so the bounded intent remains until the table next renders and then resolves current identity. Hidden panels either retain the same entity and snapshot reconciliation or are reconstructed with false/None. No stale numeric target is stored by the new application state. These combined pending-empty/collapse/hide sequences were inspected, not independently added as new dynamic tests.

Horizontal keys retain the separate horizontal offset path and do not create vertical intent. Once a reveal is consumed, wheel scrolling can leave the selected row offscreen; later passive reordering and horizontal navigation preserve that viewport. Existing coalesced bursts also mix horizontal keys with pending vertical navigation. Wheel routing and focus-navigation tests passed.

The new state is one bounded boolean, without allocation, queue, timer or polling work. It adds at most one O(process count) identity scan per render that consumes a vertical request, rather than scanning on every passive render. Existing row sizing already traverses process rows. No new race, borrow across callback, background UI access, or resource lifetime was found.

Tests enter the real accept_snapshot and key-event paths and flush coalesced frames, without directly mutating the reveal flag or asserting its implementation. The primary case explicitly puts A at the top of the row viewport, inserts two earlier rows, dispatches Up/Up, restores original rows, and asserts full selected identity, current index and actual instantiated bounds excluding the header and border. The unchanged-order control and removed/reused PID case distinguish the defect from generic layout failure. The retained actual RED has one pass/one failure and the same original regression has two passes after the correction.
